newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M says to move shares to bourse O list.
newsitem.headline: H&M says to move shares to bourse O list.

text.p: Swedish fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz said on Thursday that it planned to move its shares from the Stockholm bourse's main A list to the smaller O list due to a new tax law.
The Stockholm Stock Exchange has approved the move and Hennes & Mauritz shares will start trading on the O list on June 10, H&M said in a statement.
The move follows the parliament's adoption last week of a new law by which the owners of family-owned firms traded on the exchange's primary A list have to pay a higher wealth tax.

H&M's capital is about 38 percent owned by Stefan Persson and his family and the family controls about 70 percent of the voting rights. Persson's father founded the company which has been listed since 1974.
H&M said it had considered moving abroad but this share shift was an alternative.
H&M shares slipped on news of the share move and were trading 19.5 crowns lower 234.5 crowns at 0945 GMT.
